headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem plus broad shell/network access; Goose’s MCP and git writes amplify the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and uses stdin/stdout plus code execution; Goose shares state via filesystem and can use MCP extensions. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled files the other later parses. The pathway is not guaranteed by default, but it exists in common setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file content can be used as an injection bridge.
IF Goose loads MCP-produced or file-derived content into prompts without provenance checks, injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-written files.
Add a provenance prefix to any cross-agent handoff file.
Review and strip instructions from shared artifacts before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read/write filesystem access, and both touch user-provided files or application data. Goose explicitly handles extension-specific tokens and MCP extensions, while AutoGen handles model provider API keys. Shared files or logs can therefore expose sensitive data across the pair in default-style workflows, though not necessarily uncontrollably.
conditions: IF either agent writes secrets or prompts into the shared workspace, the other can read them.
IF logs or transcripts are stored in the same directory, sensitive data can be copied into outputs.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Rotate any keys that may have been written to disk.
Separate logs per agent and restrict permissions.
Delete transient transcripts after each run.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands; Goose also modifies git state and shares state via filesystem. In a shared repo or cwd, concurrent writes and git operations can race and overwrite each other, causing irreversible repository corruption or lost work. AutoGen lacks git writes, but the overlap on writable files is enough to make the conflict dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or cwd, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Goose performs git operations while AutoGen edits files in the same tree, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate clone or directory.
Serialize file writes with a lock file.
Disable git mutations for Goose during shared runs.
Snapshot the workspace before parallel execution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Goose can consume files, MCP outputs, and shell results as part of coding workflows. If Goose treats AutoGen-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes, package installs, or shell actions. The pair’s default-style automation makes this a high-blast-radius pathway.
conditions: IF Goose uses AutoGen-generated text as a task specification, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF AutoGen emits unverified facts into files that Goose later executes or commits, errors cascade into persistent changes.
mitigations: Require human review before any file write or shell action.
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted by default.
Add a verification step before Goose executes generated instructions.
Keep generated plans separate from executable scripts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is operational: both handle secrets and user files, so a mismatch could arise if the operator routes regulated data through them, but the profiles do not prove a specific violation. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, both agents may process it.
IF the operator requires a specific residency or retention policy, neither profile documents one here.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Document retention and deletion steps before use.
Keep secrets in a separate vault.
Review vendor/compliance terms before deployment.
